Muhammad Tayyab's Final Year Project is called 'AI Smart Scrum Pro' — an intelligent, AI-powered Scrum Project Management Platform built on the MERN stack with a custom fine-tuned NLP model for automated user story generation. It is a comprehensive, role-based Agile/Scrum project management web application that leverages Artificial Intelligence to automate and enhance the software development lifecycle. The platform serves four distinct user roles — Client, Project Lead, Scrum Master, and Developer — each with tailored dashboards, workflows, and permissions. This is his strongest project, his favorite project, and his most impressive work.

The standout feature of Tayyab's FYP is a custom fine-tuned FLAN-T5 (Google) NLP model with LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) adapters that automatically converts raw client requirements into structured User Stories and Module Breakdowns. The base model is google/flan-t5-base (Sequence-to-Sequence Transformer), fine-tuned using LoRA via HuggingFace PEFT library with PyTorch. The model takes raw client requirement text as input and outputs structured user stories in the format 'As a [role], I want [feature], so that [benefit]' along with acceptance criteria, priority levels, and module breakdowns. Generation parameters include max_length=512, temperature=0.7, top_p=0.92, and repetition_penalty=1.1. This is NOT a pre-built API call — it's a custom-trained model, which is a key differentiator.

The AI Smart Scrum Pro FYP addresses major gaps in traditional Scrum tools like Jira, Trello, and Azure DevOps. These existing tools require manual conversion of client requirements into user stories (time-consuming and error-prone), need separate tools for different Scrum activities, have no AI-driven developer recommendation or progress prediction, and have limited role-based workflows. Tayyab's platform solves all these problems by providing a unified, AI-enhanced platform that automates requirement analysis, recommends developers based on skills and performance, monitors progress with health scores, and manages the full Scrum lifecycle in one place.

The FYP tech stack is extensive. Frontend: React 19.2.0, Vite 6.4.1, React Router DOM 7, TailwindCSS 3.4.18, Framer Motion, Recharts (charts), Material-UI, Lucide React (icons), Axios, React Hook Form, React Toastify, drag-and-drop libraries, jsPDF and xlsx for report exports, mammoth and pdfjs-dist for document parsing. Backend: Node.js, Express.js, MongoDB with Mongoose, JWT authentication, bcryptjs, Helmet.js, CORS, rate limiting, compression, Morgan logging, Multer file uploads, Nodemailer, Express Validator. AI/ML: Python 3, PyTorch, HuggingFace Transformers, PEFT for LoRA, FLAN-T5-Base. Database: MongoDB Atlas. Total: 20 frontend + 13 backend + 4 AI production dependencies.

The FYP has 5 user roles with distinct dashboards. Client: submits requirements (text or file upload), reviews AI-generated user stories, provides sprint review feedback with multi-dimensional ratings. Project Lead: manages product backlog, gets AI-powered developer recommendations with confidence scores, monitors AI progress with health scores and burndown analysis, manages task assignment, generates reports with PDF/Excel export, uses Kanban sprint board. Scrum Master: manages sprints, schedules Scrum ceremonies (planning, standups, reviews, retrospectives), monitors blockers with SLA tracking, documents meeting minutes, manages team workload, views analytics dashboard. Developer: views personal tasks, logs time, submits daily standups, reports blockers, joins meetings, uses personal Kanban board.

Key features of the FYP include: AI-powered requirement-to-user-story generation from text or file uploads (.docx, .pdf, .txt), sprint management with burndown tracking and velocity calculation, rich task management with subtasks, comments with likes and replies, time logging, file attachments, and AI-recommended developer assignment with confidence scores. Blocker management with full lifecycle tracking, severity levels, SLA indicators, and AI resolution suggestions. Scrum ceremony scheduling with calendar grid, recurrence options, attendance tracking, and auto-creation of meeting minutes. Meeting minutes with retro templates and action items. Notification system. Developer recommendation engine based on skills, workload, and performance. Reports with velocity charts, burndown charts, and workload distribution exportable to PDF and Excel. Client feedback system with sentiment detection and AI analysis.

The scale of Tayyab's FYP is impressive: approximately 169 frontend files and 136 backend files. It contains 34 React pages across 7 role-based directories, 107+ reusable React components, 13 API service files on the frontend, 16 backend controllers, 14 API route files, 15 Mongoose database models, 3 middleware files, and approximately 63 AI model files for the fine-tuned FLAN-T5 with LoRA adapters. The application uses React Context API for state management, React Router DOM v7 for routing with role-based access control, TailwindCSS with custom color palette and 10+ custom animations, and comprehensive security measures including JWT authentication, bcrypt password hashing, Helmet.js security headers, rate limiting, CORS, and input validation.

The AI pipeline in Tayyab's FYP works as follows: (1) Client submits requirements via the Submit Requirements page using text input or file upload. (2) File content is extracted client-side using mammoth for .docx and pdfjs-dist for .pdf files. (3) Node.js backend calls the Python AI service via stdin/stdout inter-process communication (IPC). (4) The Python service loads the FLAN-T5 base model and applies the custom LoRA adapter. (5) The model generates user stories in natural language, which are parsed into structured JSON format. (6) Each story includes storyText, acceptanceCriteria, and priority. (7) Modules are extracted and linked to the stories. (8) Results are stored in MongoDB and presented to the Client for approval or rejection. The backend also features an AI developer recommendation engine that matches developers to tasks based on skills, availability, workload, and historical performance data with a confidence score.
